title: Granger Causal Chain Discovery for Sepsis-Associated Derangements via Continuous-Time Hawkes Processes

problem.claim: Continuous EMR surveillance seeks to identify adverse events early, but many events such as sepsis lack elucidated prodromes that can support early interception.

gap.claim: A clinically relevant and interpretable framework is needed to infer temporal interactions among EMR features and identify patterns preceding and specific to impending adverse events.

contributions.claim: A linear multivariate Hawkes process model with a ReLU link function is proposed to recover a Granger Causal graph containing exciting and inhibiting effects.
A scalable two-phase gradient-based method is developed to obtain a maximum surrogate-likelihood estimator.
The method is extended to patient data from the Grady hospital system to identify interpretable Granger Causal chains preceding sepsis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The two-phase gradient-based method is reported to be effective through extensive numerical simulation.
Application to the Grady hospital data is reported to identify several highly interpretable Granger Causal chains preceding sepsis.
The implementation code is reported as available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Automated EMR surveillance is increasing, but sepsis and other adverse events often lack known prodromal chains for early intervention.
Interpretability requires modeling temporal interactions among multiple EMR features and detecting event-specific precursors.
The work proposes a ReLU-linked multivariate Hawkes process for recovering Granger Causal graphs with excitatory and inhibitory effects.
A scalable two-phase gradient method estimates the model and is evaluated through numerical simulation.
The method is applied to Grady hospital patient data, where the estimated graph identifies interpretable chains preceding sepsis.

source_observation.claim: The approach models temporal interactions across multiple EMR features and represents both exciting and inhibiting effects in a Granger Causal graph.

interpretation.claim: Interpretable event-chain discovery may benefit from explicitly modeling signed temporal influence rather than only positive associations.

application.claim: For longitudinal clinical monitoring, consider signed temporal-interaction models when the goal is to identify actionable precursor chains.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this modeling choice generalizes beyond the reported sepsis setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the EMR feature set, preprocessing, cohort size, or prediction horizon.
The abstract does not provide quantitative simulation or clinical performance results.
The abstract does not describe baselines, ablations, or validation procedures.
